A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COIR benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine retrieval models, including benchmark scores, latency measurements, and input-length experiments in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds BM25 evaluations and results on candidate datasets in Appendix A and Table 7.

M1.justification: The benchmark's query/corpus construction and dense retrieval procedures remain unchanged, including code-context segmentation, pooling, and cosine ranking. Newly documented cleaning procedures do not establish a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: The ten-dataset COIR suite and its tasks remain unchanged. Appendix A and Table 7 add auxiliary evaluations on Human-eval, mbpp, and sampled XcodeEval data, which are excluded from the suite as insufficiently challenging.

E2.justification: BM25 is added to the main comparison in Table 3, alongside all nine retained retrievers. The four models in the new Table 7 use checkpoints already represented in v1; CodeRAG-Bench appears only in the benchmark overview.

E3.justification: The new dataset-screening evaluation specifies NDCG@10 and a 13k XcodeEval sample. Existing splits, input limits, ranking procedures, and the 512-versus-4096-token experiment remain unchanged. Appendix A's cleaning descriptions do not establish that the retained experiments used revised data.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands benchmark-validation analyses: Figure 3 examines performance dispersion, Section 5.5 and Figure 4 analyze CodeSearchNet-versus-COIR score gaps, and Appendix A/Table 7 examine whether candidate datasets distinguish models. The earlier efficiency, input-length, and BEIR-ranking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 introduces boxplots and explicit comparisons of performance variation across datasets, adding descriptive statistical reporting absent from v1. This is between-dataset dispersion, not repeated-run uncertainty; neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The nine original Table 3 rows and Tables 4–6 retain their numerical results. v2 adds BM25 scores, including a 29.79 average, and twelve candidate-dataset scores in Table 7. Section 5.1 corrects Voyage-Code-002's stated average from 52.86 to 56.26, matching the table already present in v1; this is not a performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix C retains the same DCG, IDCG, NDCG, and weighted Jaccard definitions. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new empirical analyses introduce no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add claims that existing models overfit leaderboards and emphasize LLM-based retrieval as a promising direction. COIR is additionally positioned as mitigating overfitting, with explicit first-comprehensive-benchmark and manual-curation contributions, extending v1's focus on coverage, difficulty, and usability.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly interprets score gaps as overfitting and E5-Mistral's small gap as evidence that LLM-based retrieval reduces it. Figure 3's discussion connects dispersion with robustness, while Appendix E explains that retrieved answers can be intermediate strategies or solution components. The original three limitations are retained and moved to Section 7.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents hash-based deduplication and filtering of inadequate code descriptions, without removal counts demonstrating changed datasets. v2 adds the StackOverflow license, replaces the project link with an anonymous review link, and shortens pip install coir-eval to the incomplete pip install. Hardware, software versions, and existing resource tables are retained.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from addressing limited benchmark coverage to overcoming purported CodeSearchNet overfitting. Table 1 adds CodeRAG-Bench, and BM25's reference is introduced. Related work is substantially condensed, dropping discussion and citations including ColBERT, COIL, and RetroMAE, while strengthening explicit novelty claims.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, desiderata, and conclusion are extensively rewritten or condensed. v2 introduces a contribution list, regroups task descriptions, moves limitations and licenses into main-text sections, and adds appendices on curation, realism, and innovation. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column formatting, with widespread table and float rearrangement. v2 adds boxplots, a score-gap chart, and the candidate-dataset results table; expands Tables 1 and 3; and reformats and relocates retained example and resource tables. Figures 1–2 retain their content.

improvement.justification: BM25 supplies a useful missing lexical reference, and the new curation descriptions and candidate-dataset results better explain benchmark selection. However, Section 5.5 elevates differences between CodeSearchNet and a heterogeneous aggregate into central overfitting claims without controls establishing that explanation. The new screening evaluation is underspecified, and the installation command loses its package name. These gains and weaknesses affect important aspects of the paper, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
